question: Which remaining skill-ecosystem contract should OpenClaw standardize first: install-time trust metadata, trigger/routing metadata, publishing-service reliability, or agent-pack composition?
rationale: The remaining work defines public SKILL.md/ClawHub semantics and trust boundaries; code inspection shows partial implementations but no single narrow source-level bug that automation can safely fix.

options.title: Scope trust metadata first
options.body: Standardize an audit-only skill permission/provenance contract and leave enforcement, trigger metadata, and agent packs as separate follow-ups.

options.title: Split by lifecycle stage
options.body: Break this umbrella into discovery, publishing, trust, trigger, and composition trackers, each with a named owner and acceptance proof.

options.title: Move service-only work out
options.body: Keep only missing OpenClaw API/security seams here and route ClawHub publishing-service bugs to the ClawHub owner repo or service backlog.

recommendation.title: Scope trust metadata first
recommendation.body: Standardize an audit-only skill permission/provenance contract and leave enforcement, trigger metadata, and agent packs as separate follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is product/security scope across OpenClaw core and ClawHub, and steipete is tied to the current vision and skills CLI history.
